title: Early-warning eval hooks for version-lock events
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Background: When a model version is pinned in the catalog or by a customer, subtle regressions can surface quickly in production. We need an always-on, fast feedback mechanism that runs a lightweight set of checks immediately after a pin/upgrade event (catalog edits, customer locks, or promotion to dedicated/private). Goal: surface high-confidence regressions with low latency so operators and customers can take action before broad exposure.

Scope and proposal: Implement an "early-warning eval hook" subsystem that subscribes to pin/change events in the catalog and customer pin API and triggers a prioritized, lightweight eval job. The hook will: 
- Run a small, curated smoke suite (10–50 short prompts) chosen per-model and per-customer profile.
- Execute in a fast-path evaluation tier (low-cost instances or priority queue) with timeout of ~30s.
- Emit graded signals: PASS / WARN / FAIL with confidence scores and sampled examples.
- If WARN/FAIL, escalate by creating a ticket in a monitoring workspace, notifying the owning PM/SE, and optionally block non-critical rollouts until acknowledged.

Differentiators vs full preflight: this is intentionally small and fast — not a full gated eval. It must be cheap enough to trigger on many events (catalog edits, customer-initiated locks, CI promotions) while still catching major quality regressions (hallucination spikes, toxicity, classification flips on targeted test-cases).

Operational requirements:
- Hooks must be idempotent and safe to re-run (retries if infra errors).
- Sample selection should mix global smoke prompts and customer-owned probes (if the customer has a stored probe-set).
- Configurable thresholds per-catalog-model and per-customer to reduce noise.
- Audit trail: store results, payload, model hash, and pin metadata in the eval store for postmortem and metric analysis.

Cost/coverage trade-offs: we will tune the smoke size by default to minimize cost; customers can opt-in to larger suites. We'll track precision/recall of the early-warning tier versus full evals and adjust sampling ratios accordingly.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Hook subscribes to catalog/model-pin and customer-pin change events and reliably receives events in staging and prod (less than 30s delivery lag).
A2: Smoke suite runner executes within timeout budget and returns a structured PASS/WARN/FAIL verdict with example traces for each evaluation (latency median < 12s).
A3: Results are stored with model version hash, event id, and customer id in the eval store and visible in a lightweight console panel.
A4: WARN/FAIL cases create an incident/ticket with links to the eval run and notify configured Slack channels and on-call rotation.
A5: Admins can adjust per-model and per-customer thresholds without redeploying the hook service.
decisions: D1: Reuse existing probe-runner service for smoke execution with a new 'fast-path' priority queue instead of building a separate runner.
D2: Default smoke suite size = 20 prompts; allow customer override via pin metadata (max 100).
D3: First-tier notifications are INFO->WARN->FAIL escalation using configured severity mapping; no automatic global rollback at launch (only suggestions and manual rollback UI).
D4: Store full run artifacts for 30 days in the eval store; aggregate metrics exported to Grafana for long-term trends.
